extracted_by: hand, T-0313 — the Democrat read, April 1834
note: Vol. I No. 21, the lightest of the five and the one whose page 3 the segmenter cuts hardest: twelve of thirty-two columns carry the fallback banner, but the Vision-read columns of page 3 are cut so far left or right that most advertisements survive as half-lines of five or six characters. The town is therefore read narrowly here — the corner of Dearborn and Lake for the fourth time in the month, the timber arrangement with A. McGregor, the marine list, and the Hennepin letter list, which is recorded and NOT minted. Page 4 is a Waldie's Circulating Library prospectus and a Knickerbocker prospectus across six of its eight columns and carries no town claim.

claims.notes: THE LIST T-0313'S OWN BRIEF CALLED APRIL'S, and it is not Chicago's — it is the post office at HENNEPIN, in Putnam County, whose uncalled-for letters the Democrat ran as it ran other out-of-county lists. Chicago's April list is in the first two issues of the month and is minted there (1834-04-01 c001, c002). No name here is minted: a Hennepin letter mints a Hennepin resident candidate and this corpus is a register of THIS town, which is the call T-0290 made for the Hennepin list of July 1834 and T-0292 for the Hennepin and Plainfield lists of October. The same list runs at 1834-04-16 and 1834-04-30, so it stood for at least three weeks; each printing is recorded where it stands.

The 1834-04-30 printing of the same notice reads the length `[fro]m 12 to 60 [ft] in length` at its line 3132 and is signed two lines below by `[P.] PRUYNE & CO.`, which is why the claim is compiled onto that house; the signature is not in THIS quote and no proprietor is minted from it. `Mr. A. McGregor` is cut here to `A. M Gregor` in the other half of the same printed lines at page 3 column 3 line 2791 and is not minted either, for the same reason. The placement carried on the business is Pruyne's own, from the 1834-04-08 reading of their store heading, and is not claimed by these lines.

claims.notes: Two entries, and the second is the Westward Ho clearing for St. Joseph again — her fourth appearance in the month's four marine lists. The arrival is from CLEVELAND, which is a lower-lake port and not the St. Joseph shuttle: April 1834 is the month the long-haul season opened, and the 1834-04-16 editorial's five vessels on passage from the east are the same fact from the other end. The schooner's name reads `Predest Sweet` and is given as `[Prudence] Sweet` in brackets; the second arrival's name is cut entirely.

business.name: J. K. Botsford
business.trade: grocer and dealer in hardware, tin ware and stoves

claims.notes: WINDOW SASH CAME FROM DETROIT BY THE FACTORY, and two Chicago houses were keeping it in stock in April 1834 — this one and John H. Kinzie, whose warehouse advertisement opposite the fort names the same article a week earlier. That is a fabric fact about the buildings the town was raising that same month: their windows were bought made, not joined here. The dateline of 22 April and the position of these lines in the column put them in the same advertisement as c002 and c003, so the claim is compiled onto that house; the goods, not the placement, are what these three lines add.
